authors.name: Donella Meadows
authors.summary: A systems thinker and teacher whose practical writing makes feedback, leverage, and system behaviour legible.
notes: Return to the leverage-points essay when a problem looks like a list of isolated symptoms.

relatedAuthors.reason: Both treat leverage as a property of relationships inside a whole system.

authors.name: Ursula K. Le Guin
authors.summary: A novelist, poet, essayist, and translator who used imagined societies to test assumptions about power, gender, freedom, and belonging.
notes: Her worlds are useful as thought experiments because their social arrangements stay complicated rather than becoming slogans.

relatedAuthors.reason: Both make social systems visible by changing the frame through which they are examined.

authors.name: Christopher Alexander
authors.summary: An architect and design theorist concerned with patterns, wholeness, and environments that can grow through participation.
notes: The pattern idea is most useful here as a language for relationships, not as a catalogue of recipes.

relatedAuthors.reason: Brand extends Alexander's concern for living, adaptable places into maintenance and time.

authors.name: Stewart Brand
authors.summary: A writer and project-builder whose work follows long time horizons, adaptive buildings, tools, and institutional learning.
notes: Pair the building layers with system feedback: different parts need different rates of change.

relatedAuthors.reason: Both argue for design that can adapt through use rather than resist change.
Pace layers and feedback loops offer complementary ways to see change in complex systems.

authors.name: Andy Matuschak
authors.summary: A researcher and designer exploring tools that help people remember, understand, and develop ideas over time.
notes: The working notes are as important as the polished essays because they expose the links between ideas.

relatedAuthors.reason: Both explore linked notes and tools for thought as cultural and interface practices.

authors.name: Maggie Appleton
authors.summary: A designer and anthropologist creating visual essays about programming, culture, and the ways people cultivate knowledge online.
notes: Follow the digital-garden trail when thinking about a public atlas that can remain unfinished and useful.

relatedAuthors.reason: Both use public, evolving notes to explore how digital tools shape understanding.
